title: Studiewinkel — Audit

cro.summary: The technical audit shows a moderate Lighthouse performance score (49) and missing structured data, which has a direct impact on organic reach and trust in search results. No product schemas, AggregateRating, or breadcrumbs were detected, so the store is missing opportunities for free Google Shopping appearance and stars in SERPs. Checkout could not be fully probed due to a 404 error, which is itself a serious risk signal.
topActions: Add Product and AggregateRating schema on all PDPs so stars become visible in Google search results and the store qualifies for Google Shopping
Investigate and fix the 404 on the checkout page — an inaccessible checkout is a hard conversion blocker that costs revenue
Improve the Lighthouse performance score from 49 to at least 70 through load-time optimisations (image compression, remove render-blocking scripts) to reduce bounces caused by slow page construction

phases.name: Foundation Fix
actions: Investigate and fix the 404 on the checkout page: check Magento 2 router config, URL rewrites, and any custom checkout module; place a test order on mobile and desktop to confirm the full checkout path works

Implement Consent Mode v2 via GTM: add google_consent_defaults with analytics_storage and ad_storage set to 'denied', connect to the existing CMP or implement a simple cookie banner — this restores modelled conversion data for Google campaigns from users without consent

Activate Meta Conversions API (CAPI) server-side alongside the browser pixel: connect via Magento 2 backend events on purchase, add_to_cart, and initiate_checkout so iOS-blocked and ad-blocker-missed conversions are still passed through
Run a pixels audit via GTM Preview Mode and Meta Events Manager: confirm which conversion events actually fire on the thank-you page and close gaps in the purchase-event implementation

Raise the DMARC policy from 'quarantine' to 'reject' once Flowmailer reports confirm that all legitimate mail streams authenticate correctly — eliminates remaining spoofing risk and increases domain trust with Gmail and Microsoft 365
phases.objective: Close the three hard blockers — broken checkout, missing tracking data, and missing ad signals — so the platform is steerable again and no longer loses revenue through technical gaps
phases.expectedOutcome: Checkout 404 resolved and testable, attribution loss reduced from 45% to under 20%, Google and Meta campaigns receive full conversion signals, ROAS reporting accurate

phases.name: Acceleration
actions: Implement Product schema (JSON-LD) on all PDPs including price, availability, and SKU — this makes the store eligible for Google Shopping free listings and rich product results
Add AggregateRating schema on PDPs based on existing reviews — stars appear in organic search results, with an expected direct CTR uplift of 15–30% on product landing pages
Add BreadcrumbList schema site-wide for better SERP navigation display and internal link equity

Implement a server-side Google Tag Manager (sGTM) endpoint: increases cookie lifetime, reduces browser-side blocking, and extends attribution windows for all connected channels including Google Ads and GA4

Run a Lighthouse optimisation pass aimed at lifting the score from 49 to 70+: prioritise render-blocking JavaScript via a RequireJS audit, image compression to WebP, and lazy loading — the Speed Index of 14s and TTI of 35s are the main drivers
Implement a CDN (Cloudflare Free or Pro) in front of the Apache origin: addresses the 384ms TTFB, distributes static assets via edge nodes, and structurally lowers Time to Interactive
phases.objective: Increase organic visibility and conversion rate through structured data, server-side tracking, and Lighthouse score improvement — unlock SERP stars, Google Shopping, and better ad steering data
dependencies: Phase 1 complete: checkout works and the tracking baseline is clean
phases.expectedOutcome: Lighthouse performance above 70, Product and AggregateRating schema active and crawled, stars visible in Google SERP, sGTM operational with a full data pipeline, attribution loss under 15%

phases.name: Platform Rebuild
actions: Start a Shopify migration exploration: map Magento 2 customisations, ERP/PIM connections, and integrations to determine migration complexity — the low number of third-party scripts (2 domains) points to limited integration complexity

Migrate to Shopify with Shopify Checkout as a replacement for the current unstable custom checkout — structurally eliminates the 404 vulnerability and delivers an optimised, mobile-first checkout path
Activate Shopify Customer Events for tracking as a replacement for the GTM-only setup: structurally solves consent mode, attribution, and pixel health without depending on browser-side scripts

Build email automations in the chosen ESP: activate welcome flow, abandoned cart flow, and post-purchase flow — industry benchmark is 30% revenue contribution from email; current contribution is unknown but likely underused
Implement AI readiness: add FAQ schema, complete all 5 AI-agent data points (price, specs, reviews, shipping, availability), and ensure the Google Merchant Center feed is active and error-free
Add DKIM selectors for all separate sending sources in the SPF record (sqr.nl, Flowmailer, Exclaimer, Microsoft 365) so all mail paths are cryptographically identified
phases.objective: Migrate from the Magento 2 monolith to Shopify to resolve structural platform debt, guarantee checkout stability, and activate owned-channel automation
dependencies: Phase 1 complete: checkout and tracking baseline operational
Phase 2 complete: CDN, sGTM, and structured data active so migration does not regress the wins already achieved
phases.expectedOutcome: Shopify live with a stable checkout, Lighthouse above 80, email automations active with measurable revenue contribution, Google Merchant Center feed without errors, AI data points complete, total attribution loss under 10%

quickWins: Implement Consent Mode v2 via the existing GTM container: 1 working day, direct impact on Google campaign optimisation and modelled conversion data
Add Product schema + AggregateRating on PDPs via JSON-LD in the Magento 2 template: 1–2 working days, stars in SERP within 2–4 weeks after crawl
topPriorities: Fix the 404 on the checkout page — a broken checkout blocks all revenue from paid traffic
Implement Consent Mode v2 + Meta CAPI to reduce the 45% attribution loss and restore ad algorithms
Add Product schema + AggregateRating on PDPs for direct CTR gain in Google SERP and Google Shopping eligibility
Activate server-side tagging (sGTM) as a structural tracking fix for all channels
Evaluate and start a Shopify migration to structurally resolve Magento 2 debt, CDN absence, and checkout instability
roadmap.northStarMetric: Monthly revenue from paid channels (ROAS x ad spend) — only rises if tracking is correct, checkout converts, and the platform is stable
roadmap.executiveSummary: Studiewinkel structurally leaks ~€11,400/month from one dominant cause: 45% attribution loss in the tracking layer. Ad algorithms steer on half the data, ROAS reporting is distorted, and checkout returns a 404. In addition, all structured data is missing, so Google drops both stars and Shopping eligibility. The path forward: first close the tracking and checkout gaps so the platform knows what works, then accelerate conversion via schema and CRO, and finally rebuild the platform onto Shopify to structurally resolve Magento 2 debt and CDN absence.

deliverability.summary: Email authentication for studiewinkel.nl sits on a solid base: SPF is valid with multiple authorised sending sources, DKIM is configured, and DMARC is set to 'quarantine' with forensic reporting active via Flowmailer. The largest remaining risk is that DMARC is not yet on 'reject', so spoofing attempts can still partially get through. On the ESP side, there is no external confirmation of active email flows, which is a blind spot for owned-channel health.
topActions: Raise the DMARC policy from 'quarantine' to 'reject' once the DMARC reports via dmarc@inbound.flowmailer.net confirm that all legitimate mail streams authenticate correctly — this eliminates remaining spoofing risk and increases domain trust with major mailbox providers such as Gmail and Microsoft.

Add a DKIM selector for each separate sending source in the SPF record (sqr.nl, Flowmailer, Exclaimer, Microsoft 365) and verify that all selectors are actively signing — currently only the 'mail' selector was found, which means not all sending paths are cryptographically identified.

Determine which ESP manages transactional and commercial email flows and validate that welcome flow, abandoned cart, and post-purchase automations are active — the absence of this data from the outside is a signal that the owned channel may be underused versus the industry standard of 30% email revenue contribution.

adBounceRevenue.summary: Post-click bounce sits at the 45% baseline — there is no technically driven bounce uplift measurable, and mobile page performance is good (LCP 814ms, INP 128ms, CLS 0.0). The largest risk sits in the tracking layer: with 45% estimated attribution loss, no Consent Mode, no server-side tagging, and missing pixels, the ad algorithm receives no conversion signal for nearly half of clicks, which leads to structurally under-steered campaigns and wasted budget.
topActions: Implement Consent Mode v2 (via Google Tag Manager) so the Google algorithm also receives modelled conversion data from users without consent — this is the fastest step to reduce the 45% attribution loss and restore campaign optimisation.

Activate Meta Conversions API (CAPI) server-side alongside the browser pixel: this still passes through conversions missed by ad blockers or iOS restrictions, with a direct impact on Meta campaign performance and ROAS reporting.

Run a pixels audit via GTM Preview and Meta Events Manager to confirm which conversion events actually fire on the thank-you page — the 'missing' pixels-health status points to a gap between the tracking plan and the live implementation.
Evaluate server-side tagging (sGTM) as a structural fix: this raises data quality platform-wide, reduces dependence on browser cookies, and extends attribution windows for all connected channels.

keyWins: Replacing the Magento 2 monolith with Shopify Liquid structurally addresses the low Lighthouse score (49) via better script architecture
Shopify Checkout replaces the current broken or custom checkout (404 response) and raises conversion rate through native payment methods and one-page checkout
Shopify Customer Events + server-side tagging via Shopify significantly reduce the estimated 45% attribution loss
No CDN on the current platform — Shopify's global CDN delivers immediate performance and TTFB improvement (current TTFB 384ms)
shopifyMigration.summary: The prospect is likely running Magento 2 as a monolith without a CDN, with a notably strong mobile CWV score but a Lighthouse performance of only 49. The tracking setup has substantial gaps (45% estimated attribution loss, no Consent Mode, no server-side tagging) that are directly addressable on Shopify with Customer Events and Checkout Extensibility.
keyRisks: Magento 2 custom work (ERP connections, custom modules, B2B pricing rules) is not visible in the audit but can raise migration complexity substantially
Checkout flow could not be tested due to a 404 error — unclear whether a complex custom checkout or payment-provider integration sits behind it that is hard to migrate
shopifyMigration.rationale: Magento 2 as a monolith without a CDN is a platform that will fall short on scalability and maintenance cost over time, but the mobile CWV scores are surprisingly good (LCP 814ms, INP 128ms, CLS 0.0). The Lighthouse score of 49, however, points to deeper structural issues (likely render-blocking JS via RequireJS and Magento's own script architecture) that Shopify Liquid would solve without needing Hydrogen. The checkout path returned a 404, which may mean checkout is custom or broken — a direct migration driver toward Shopify's optimised checkout. Tracking is the strongest business case: no Consent Mode, no server-side tagging, and an estimated 45% attribution loss are problems that Shopify Customer Events + GTM integration can significantly improve. The number of third-party scripts is minimal (2 domains, 35KB), which limits migration complexity. Major unknown: the depth of Magento custom work and ERP/PIM connections cannot be inferred from the audit.
topActions: Run a technical discovery on the Magento 2 installation: inventory custom modules, ERP/PIM connections, and checkout configuration to determine the real migration complexity
Repair or validate the checkout flow on the current platform to understand whether a custom or third-party checkout is active that must be migrated
Implement Consent Mode v2 and server-side tagging immediately (regardless of the migration decision) to push the 45% attribution loss down — this is urgent, platform-independent action

techArchitecture.summary: The webshop runs on a monolithic Magento 2 stack with no detectable CDN, which translates into a critical Lighthouse performance score of 49 and an extremely high Time to Interactive of nearly 35 seconds on mobile. Although mobile Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) currently score well, the heavy page size of 8.6 MB combined with 76 requests and a Speed Index of 14 seconds points to structural rendering debt. Server-side tracking is completely missing, which with the current GTM-only setup leads to high attribution loss.
topActions: Implement a CDN (e.g. Cloudflare or Fastly) directly in front of the Apache origin: the absence of edge caching is the most likely cause of the 384ms TTFB and the lack of static asset distribution, which structurally depresses the Speed Index of 14s and TTI of 35s.

Reduce total page size from 8.6 MB by running a JavaScript bundle audit on the Magento 2 stack: with only 5.9 KB unused JS, the weight is likely coming from large images or media — implement lazy loading and WebP conversion to lift the Lighthouse score above the critical threshold of 50.

Implement server-side tracking via Google Enhanced Conversions and Meta Conversion API (CAPI): with browser-side GTM only and no sGTM endpoint, estimated attribution loss is high, which has a direct impact on steering data for paid campaigns and retargeting audiences.

coreThesis: ~45% attribution loss in tracking — ad algorithms optimise on incomplete data, ROAS reporting is structurally too low. Estimated leakage: €11,400/mo.

ceoTriggers.kpi: ROAS drops while ad spend rises
ceoTriggers.realMeaning: The store leaks visitors before they convert. More traffic into a leaking funnel makes the problem worse.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Every extra euro in ads returns less. More budget ≠ more revenue.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: You are pouring water into a bucket with holes. We close the holes so every euro of ad spend returns more.

ceoTriggers.kpi: Mobile converts dramatically lower than desktop
ceoTriggers.realMeaning: The mobile–desktop gap is almost never a UX problem. It is a performance problem: mobile is more sensitive to load time.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Desktop converts 2–3x better than mobile, while 70%+ of traffic is mobile.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: 70% of your visitors are mobile. If that half converts this poorly, you are leaving the most money where the most traffic sits.

ceoTriggers.realMeaning: If your funnel leaks, you need more clicks per conversion — and every click costs money.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: It costs more and more to acquire a new customer. Marketing is getting more expensive.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: Your CPA is not rising only because ads are getting more expensive. Fix the store and your CPA drops — without changing your ad strategy.

ceoTriggers.kpi: Market share declining against comparable product
ceoTriggers.realMeaning: With comparable products, the store with the best buying experience wins. Speed becomes the differentiator.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Competitors with a comparable product are growing faster.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: Your product is not the problem. Your store experience is the problem. The customer goes to the store where it is easier and faster.

ceoTriggers.kpi: No organic growth despite SEO investment
ceoTriggers.alarmSignal: No ranking growth after 6 months of SEO
ceoTriggers.realMeaning: Google rewards Core Web Vitals in ranking. A slow site loses to a fast competitor.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: SEO efforts are not paying off. Rankings stagnate or decline.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: Google does not rank on content alone. They rank on experience. Your Core Web Vitals are a ranking factor — and right now they are working against you.

ceoTriggers.realMeaning: AI agents rely on structured data and API accessibility. Without that, you are invisible.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Customers ask ChatGPT/Gemini for product advice and your brand does not appear.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: In 2 years, 30%+ of product searches will start with an AI agent. If that agent cannot find you, you do not exist in that world.

ceoTriggers.kpi: Shopify app costs rise but results don't
ceoTriggers.realMeaning: Every app adds weight to the store. You pay twice: the subscription + the conversion loss the app causes.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: Every month more apps, more subscriptions, but no measurable effect on revenue.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: You pay monthly for apps that slow your store down. Some cost more in conversion loss than they deliver in functionality.
ceoTriggers.tradualSolution: Revenue Leak Audit™ — Layer 2: The Engine

ceoTriggers.realMeaning: Checkout latency and layout shifts break trust at the critical moment.
ceoTriggers.whatCeoSees: 3 out of 4 customers who add something to their cart do not check out.
ceoTriggers.tradualPitch: You already convinced the customer — they clicked 'add'. And then you lose them in checkout. That is the most expensive loss there is.

revenueLeak.methodologyNote: Heuristic estimate. Assumptions: €9,000/mo revenue, 6,000 visitors/mo, 3% CVR benchmark, €75 AOV, €3,000/mo ad spend. Based on publicly measurable signals. Use as an indication, not as a definitive audit outcome.

auditSummary: Automated outside-only scan of Magento 2 store (https://studiewinkel.nl/). 2 technical risks and 2 opportunities identified.

errorsEncountered: Checkout page returned 404 — may require items in cart

adTrafficImpact.methodologyNote: Heuristic estimate based on Google CrUX correlations (LCP/INP → bounce rate). Revenue range assumes 3,000–15,000 ad visits/month, 2% CVR, €72 AOV. Use as an indication, not as a measured benchmark.

biggestTechRisk: 45% estimated attribution loss due to tracking gaps

croObservations.estImpact: Every user who cannot reach checkout does not convert. Depending on the share of direct checkout traffic, this can block 5–15% of potential orders. Immediate fix required.
croObservations.observation: The checkout page returns a 404 error on direct access. This is a hard conversion blocker: visitors sent to checkout via a direct link, retargeting ad, or abandoned-cart email hit a dead page and leave the session without a purchase.

croObservations.estImpact: Google research shows a direct correlation between performance score and bounce rate. Improving the score from 49 to 70+ can lower bounce rate by 5–10%, which at unchanged traffic immediately sends more visitors through the funnel.
croObservations.observation: The Lighthouse performance score is 49 on desktop, which counts as 'moderate'. A slow load experience raises bounce rate substantially, especially for visitors arriving via ads. No mobile Lighthouse score was measured, but Core Web Vitals (LCP 814ms, FCP 807ms) are acceptable on their own — the gap suggests problems with JavaScript execution or resource loading outside the CWV measurements.

croObservations.estImpact: Stores with Product schema and Shopping eligibility report 20–30% more organic clicks from product-intent searches. Implementation is one-off technical work with structural traffic impact.
croObservations.observation: No Product schema was detected on product detail pages. As a result, the store does not qualify for Google Shopping appearance via organic rich results and misses price display in standard search results. This is a missed opportunity for free, high-intent traffic.

croObservations.estImpact: AggregateRating in SERPs raises CTR by 10–20% on average for product pages. With an existing organic traffic base, this immediately delivers more sessions without extra ad spend.
croObservations.observation: No AggregateRating schema is present, so review stars are missing in Google search results. Stars demonstrably raise click-through rate (CTR) and act as social proof before the visitor even enters the site. On the page itself, no review signals via schema are visible either.

croObservations.estImpact: Breadcrumb schema has a limited but measurable effect on CTR (estimated 2–5%) and helps improve crawl efficiency of large catalogues. Relatively simple implementation via an existing schema framework.
croObservations.observation: No BreadcrumbList schema was detected. Breadcrumbs in search results improve navigation clarity for users and give Google better insight into site structure, which supports indexing of category and product pages.

croObservations.estImpact: Improving the accessibility score to 85+ lowers friction for a broader audience and reduces the risk of bounces caused by unreadable or unclickable interface elements. Estimated conversion impact: 1–3% with a structural approach.
croObservations.observation: The accessibility score is 69, which means a significant part of the user interface does not meet WCAG guidelines. This affects not only users with a disability, but also SEO signals and overall mobile usability (missing alt texts, contrast ratios, form labels).

methodologyNote: Automated outside-only scan. All findings are based on publicly accessible signals: HTTP headers, DOM analysis, PageSpeed Insights API, and third-party script catalogue. No admin access used.
